design_reference: No dedicated wireframe screen — cloud-sync is infrastructure with a small status surface. Anatomy: a low-fi status pill (the design system Badge, good/bad/accent/muted tones) in a corner, reflecting the local-first store's sync state. Light theme, tokens only.

plan.goal: Make the whole app local-first and sync-aware: every write persists locally first, optionally pushes to a cloud transport in the background, and a status surface reflects the sync state — so the editor always works offline and is ready for a real backend without touching feature code.
acceptance_criteria: A CloudSyncService decorates the PersistenceService (Liskov: it IS a PersistenceService) so BookService and every feature are unchanged; it is wired once in createBrain wrapping the local store.
Writes are local-first: get/set/keys/remove hit the local store synchronously, so reads right after a write succeed and the app works fully offline.
When a cloud transport is configured, a write pushes in the background and the sync state moves idle → syncing → synced, or → error if the push fails; the local write is never lost on error.
With no transport configured the store is « offline » (local-only) and emits no per-write noise (status only changes broadcast).

Sync state changes are broadcast on the brain sync:status event; a SyncIndicator surfaces the live state, derived from a status→label/tone Record (KR-117), reading via a useSyncStatus external store (no private copy).

The SyncIndicator renders from design-system tokens/Badge (good=synced, bad=error, accent=syncing, muted=local/idle), is an aria-live status region, and is mounted once by the composition root over both routes.
View-mode/UI state is NOT synced; only the book document flows through the persistence layer (cloud-first boundary, KR-022).
plan.walking_skeleton: createCloudSyncService(local, events, transport?) decorates the local PersistenceService: local-first set (sync write) + a background transport.push that moves the status idle→syncing→synced/error and emits sync:status; with no transport it stays offline (local-only). createBrain wraps the local store with it and exposes brain.sync. useSyncStatus subscribes to sync:status; the cloud-sync feature's SyncIndicator renders the live state as a Badge pill, mounted by App over both routes. The real cloud transport (Cloudflare worker client) + offline write queue are later iterations.

iterations.goal: Real cloud transport: a CloudflareSyncService client (worker route + auth) implementing CloudTransport; debounced batched pushes; last-write-wins reconciliation on book:opened.
Offline write queue: persist pending pushes and flush on reconnect (unblocks book-creation iteration 3); surface a « N changements en attente » state.
Conflict handling: detect divergence between local and cloud, surface a resolution affordance rather than silently overwriting.

known_risks: KR-022 — pan/zoom and the canvas↔outline view-mode are UI preferences, NOT part of the synced book document; only the book flows through the persistence layer, so cloud-sync never pushes UI state (avoids spurious conflicts).
KR-011/111 — all persistence still goes through PersistenceService; CloudSyncService is a decorator over it, not a second storage surface; no raw localStorage in feature code.
KR-004 — local-first: the synchronous local write resolves before any event/navigation; the background cloud push must never block or reorder the local write.
KR-117 — the SyncStatus → label/tone mapping lives in one Record (SyncIndicator), derived not branched.

KR-114 — when the real transport lands, any cloud credential/token must be registered in persistenceKeys.ts with a SENSITIVE marker (none yet — the Cloudflare client + auth land with the Cloudflare build target).

KR-094 — the CloudTransport is selected by BUILD/PRODUCTION TARGET at the composition root (main.tsx): the local target wires a localStorage-backed LocalStorageTransport (a fake remote in a separate `cloudsync:` namespace), the Cloudflare target a worker-backed one; both implement one interface so app code is target-agnostic and tests stay offline by default. Pushes are DEBOUNCED + BATCHED (rapid writes coalesce into one push cycle; status syncing→synced/error once). book:opened triggers LAST-WRITE-WINS reconciliation by updatedAt: a newer cloud copy is adopted by writing the UNDERLYING local store (never the decorated set — avoids re-pushing what was just pulled, no echo loop) then emitting book:updated so open views re-read; a newer local copy is pushed up. Reconciliation is the only place the persistence decorator is book-aware (resolves bookKey, emits book:updated).

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: CloudSyncService is a Decorator over PersistenceService (Liskov, KR-011): createBrain wraps the local store with it and feeds it to BookService, so every feature is sync-aware with zero changes. brain.sync exposes status().

Local-first: set writes local synchronously THEN pushes in the background (KR-004); the status moves idle→syncing→synced/error and is broadcast on a new sync:status event. With no transport the store is offline (local-only) and emits nothing on writes — so the existing 99 tests are fully transparent (no async, no status noise).

useSyncStatus is an external-store subscription over sync:status (KR-013); the cloud-sync feature's SyncIndicator is a VIEW that derives label/tone from a SyncStatus Record (KR-117) and is mounted once by App over both routes.
SyncStatus is a brain type; the CloudTransport interface keeps the real backend swappable (the Cloudflare worker client is deferred).
deviations_from_plan: No real cloud transport in the skeleton — default is local-only (offline). The Cloudflare worker client, debounced batched pushes, reconciliation, the offline queue, and conflict handling are iterations 1–3.
This completes the 0.1.x MVP tier: every feature now has a walking skeleton.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — local-first delegation, offline (no transport) no-noise, idle→syncing→synced broadcast, error on push failure with the local write preserved
test_coverage.integration: SyncIndicator via brain — « Local » with no transport, syncing→synced after a write with a transport

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: Per the production-target direction: the « cloud » is selected at the composition root. The LOCAL build target wires a new LocalStorageTransport — a CloudTransport backed by a separate `cloudsync:` localStorage namespace (a fake remote) — so the full local-first machinery runs with no server; the Cloudflare build target swaps in a worker-backed transport (client + worker route + SENSITIVE auth, KR-114) via the same interface later (its CI builds around the full Cloudflare slice). createBrain stays transport-optional so tests default to offline (transparent).

CloudTransport gained an optional pull (for reconciliation). CloudSyncService now DEBOUNCES + BATCHES pushes: set() writes local synchronously then coalesces into a pending map flushed after a debounce window (default 300ms, 0 in tests); status moves syncing (synchronously on write) → synced/error once per batch; the flush timer is tracked + cleared on reschedule (timer-safe).

Last-write-wins reconciliation on book:opened (KR-094): pull the cloud copy, compare updatedAt — a newer cloud copy is adopted by writing the UNDERLYING local store (never the decorated set, so it is not re-pushed — no echo loop) then emitting book:updated so the open view re-reads; a newer local copy is pushed up; an empty cloud is seeded. This is the one place the persistence decorator is book-aware (bookKey + book:updated).
useSyncStatus/SyncIndicator unchanged (KR-013/117). No regression: with no transport (every existing test) the decorator is a transparent synchronous pass-through.
deviations_from_plan: Per user direction, the real Cloudflare client + worker route + auth are deferred to the Cloudflare build target / CI; iteration 1 delivers the transport machinery (debounce/batch + LWW reconciliation) and the local localStorage-backed transport. The Worker Route Parity checklist + KR-114 SENSITIVE token apply when that transport lands (no worker code / credential in the repo yet, so nothing un-deployable is committed).
Reconciliation is last-write-wins by updatedAt (iteration 1); divergence detection + a resolution affordance are iteration 3 (conflict handling). The offline write queue is iteration 2.

test_coverage.unit: CloudSyncService — debounced+batched push (last value per key wins, one syncing/synced), error preserves local, book:opened reconciliation both directions (adopt newer cloud + notify, push newer local up); LocalStorageTransport — push/pull round-trip + separate namespace
test_coverage.integration: SyncIndicator via brain — « Local » offline, syncing→synced after a debounced write

open_questions: Cloudflare worker route + auth shape for the real transport (iteration 1) — must follow the Worker Route Parity checklist.
Reconciliation/conflict policy (iterations 1/3) and the offline queue that unblocks book-creation iteration 3 (iteration 2).
